content_html:
Laminate flooring handles light damp cleaning, not standing water. The goal is to remove grit that scratches and use a well-wrung mop so moisture does not soak into seams.

Remove grit first

Sand and small grit act like sandpaper under a mop. If vacuuming, use a hard-floor setting without an aggressive rotating brush.

Use very little water

Dampen a microfiber mop and wring it until it does not drip. Work in sections and wipe up any puddle immediately.

Avoid steam unless specifically approved

Heat and moisture can penetrate seams and swell the core of some laminate floors. Follow the flooring brand's instructions before using a steam mop.

Spot-clean without scraping

For sticky spots, put a compatible cleaner on a cloth and work locally. Blades, scouring pads, and waxes can damage the wear layer or leave residue. If streaks remain after drying, do not add more product. Make a final pass with a barely damp mop and clean water, because excess cleaner can leave a film that attracts more soil.
